meta.title: Roots & Words — domain-clustered vocabulary dataset
meta.organizing_principle: Roots selected by measured productivity across a GRE-level corpus, then grouped into 13 semantic domains defined for this project. Grouping and ordering are original to this dataset.
meta.content_note: Root-to-meaning mappings are factual linguistic data. All definitions, example sentences, domain groupings, and notes are original work written for this project. No text from any published vocabulary book is reproduced.

words.definition: A person's sense of their own importance or identity.
words.example: Winning the award did nothing to shrink his already sizable ego.

words.definition: Someone preoccupied with their own interests above everyone else's.
words.example: As an egoist, she measured every plan by what it would do for her.

words.definition: A person who talks about themselves constantly and boastfully.
words.example: The egotist steered every conversation back to his own achievements.

words.definition: Seeing the world only from one's own point of view.
words.example: Toddlers are naturally egocentric and slowly learn to consider others.

words.definition: Marked by an obsessive preoccupation with oneself.
words.example: His egomaniacal need for praise drained the whole team.

words.definition: A second self; a trusted friend or a contrasting side of one's character.
words.example: On stage she became her flamboyant alter ego, nothing like her quiet daytime self.

words.definition: Unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
words.example: Her altruism showed in the years she spent volunteering for nothing.

words.definition: A person who puts others' needs before their own.
words.example: A true altruist, he gave away most of what he earned.

words.definition: Motivated by care for others rather than personal gain.
words.example: Their altruistic decision cost them money but helped the whole village.

words.definition: A person who dislikes and avoids other people.
words.example: The old misanthrope kept his gate locked and his neighbors at a distance.

words.definition: Disliking or shunning other people.
words.example: Her misanthropic streak made large parties a form of torture.

words.definition: Showing hatred or contempt for women.
words.example: His misogynous remarks finally cost him his position.

words.definition: Hatred of marriage.
words.example: His misogamy was so firm that he skipped every wedding he was invited to.

words.definition: Having only one spouse or partner at a time.
words.example: Swans are famously monogamous, often pairing for life.

words.definition: Involving marriage to two people at the same time.
words.example: Their bigamous arrangement collapsed the moment the paperwork surfaced.

words.definition: Having more than one spouse at once.
words.example: The documentary followed a polygamous community in the desert.

words.definition: The custom of one man having several wives.
words.example: Polygyny, one husband with many wives, appears in several old texts.

words.definition: Having more than one husband at a time.
words.example: The polyandrous household divided its labor among three husbands.

words.definition: Relating to the study of humankind.
words.example: The museum's anthropological exhibits traced tools across ten thousand years.

words.definition: The desire to help others, expressed especially through generous giving.
words.example: Her philanthropy funded scholarships for hundreds of first-generation students.

words.definition: A person who lives with strict self-discipline, avoiding comfort and pleasure.
words.example: The ascetic slept on a bare floor and ate one simple meal a day.

words.definition: A lifestyle of severe self-denial, often for spiritual reasons.
words.example: His asceticism meant no luxuries, no idle time, and few possessions.

words.definition: Skillful with the hands; nimble.
words.example: The dexterous surgeon tied the knot with a single graceful motion.

words.definition: Able to use both hands equally well.
words.example: Being ambidextrous, she could write a note with either hand.

words.definition: The ability to use both hands with equal skill.
words.example: His ambidexterity made him unpredictable on the tennis court.

words.definition: Suggesting evil or that something harmful is likely to happen.
words.example: A sinister figure lingered in the shadows at the end of the alley.

words.definition: Clever and skillful, especially in handling situations.
words.example: She gave an adroit answer that satisfied both sides of the dispute.

words.definition: Cleverness or skill in dealing with things.
words.example: He negotiated the merger with quiet adroitness.

words.definition: Lacking social grace; awkward or tactless.
words.example: It felt gauche to ask about salary at the dinner party.

words.definition: An awkward or tactless act; social clumsiness.
words.example: Interrupting the toast was a gaucherie he regretted at once.

words.definition: A person who is energized by solitude and inward reflection.
words.example: As an introvert, he recharged with a quiet evening and a book.

words.definition: An outgoing person who thrives on social interaction.
words.example: The extrovert lit up the moment the room filled with people.

words.definition: A person balanced between introversion and extroversion.
words.example: An ambivert, she enjoyed parties but needed quiet days to recover.

words.definition: The branch of medicine dealing with children.

words.definition: Relating to old age or its medical care.

words.example: She raised the binoculars to watch the hawk circling overhead.

words.example: The old pedagogue drilled Latin verbs into every reluctant student.

words.definition: The method and practice of teaching.
words.example: Her pedagogy relied on questions rather than lectures.

words.definition: To introduce a substance into the body to build immunity.
words.example: The clinic will inoculate every child before the school year begins.

words.definition: Relating to the mind or mental processes.
words.example: The injury healed quickly, but the psychological scars lasted years.

words.definition: Relating to the mind, or to supposed powers beyond the physical.
words.example: She felt a strange psychic connection to her twin.

words.definition: A method of treating the mind by exploring unconscious thoughts.
words.example: Psychoanalysis led her to memories she had long buried.

words.definition: A therapist trained in exploring the unconscious mind.
words.example: The psychoanalyst listened as the patient described a recurring dream.

words.definition: Showing the traits of a severe antisocial personality.
words.example: His psychopathic calm during the crisis unnerved everyone.

words.definition: The treatment of mental disorders through talking rather than drugs.
words.example: Months of psychotherapy gave her tools to manage the anxiety.

words.example: The headaches were psychosomatic, easing whenever the stress lifted.

words.definition: Originating in the mind rather than the body.
words.example: Doctors concluded the paralysis was psychogenic, with no physical cause.

words.example: She trained in osteopathy after a back injury of her own.

words.definition: The practice of treating disorders through manual spinal adjustment.

words.example: Years of chiropody kept the marathon runner on her feet.
